item.title: Radon measures in the Berkovich space and generically stable measures in ACVF
item.description: arXiv:2610.20758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study Keisler measures in models of ACVF. We give analogue definitions for a Keisler measure to be orthogonal to the value group and stably dominated using unique extensions, in the spirit of invariant types. Our first theorem shows that a global $M$-invariant Keisler measure is generically stable if and only if it is orthogonal to the value group if and only if it is stably dominated. This theorem is later applied to prove that for a projective variety $X$ defined over a spherically complete model $M$ of ACVF whose value group is $\mathbb R$, there is a one-to-one correspondance between the generically stable measures centered on $X$ and the Radon measures on its Berkovich analyfication of $X$. Such theorem is a measure-theoretic extension of the celebrated work of Hrushovski-Loeser, which establishes a correspondence between generically stable types with the points of the Berkovich analyfication $X^{an}$ of a projective variety$X$. As an application, normalized Chambert-Loir measures associated with semipositive continuous metrics naturally give rise examples of generically stable Keisler measures.
item.dc:creator: Alf Onshuus, Mariana Vicaria

item.title: Duality Theory for Sequent Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.20956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequent algebras were introduced by D. Vakarelov \cite{VakarelovSequentALg} as a generalization of contact algebras, replacing the binary contact relation with a relation between finite sets of regions and regions. In this paper, we present sequent algebras as Boolean algebras endowed with a finitary closure operator satisfying four conditions. We study the irreducible closed sets of these operators, which coincide with Vakarelov's clans, and use them to develop a topological representation theory for sequent algebras. We introduce the categories of sequent algebras and sequent spaces and establish a dual equivalence between them, as well as a restricted dual equivalence for morphisms preserving the full Boolean structure. We also characterize sequent congruences in terms of positive filters and minimally decreasing closed subsets of the associated sequent spaces. Finally, we show that the category of sequent algebras with sequent homomorphisms is topological over the category of Boolean algebras, obtaining completeness and cocompleteness and a complete lattice structure on the sequent structures over each Boolean algebra.
item.dc:creator: Sergio A. Celani, William Zuluaga

item.title: Local definable $(p,q)$-theorem and a refinement
item.description: arXiv:2610.21738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the definable $(p,q)$-conjecture for NIP formulas in arbitrary first-order theories. We also prove a refinement and apply it to dense pairs.
item.dc:creator: Gareth John Boxall, Charlotte Kestner, Tsinjo Rakotonarivo

item.title: Discrete Temporal CSPs et al
item.description: arXiv:2610.21967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the complexity classification of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) for first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$, established by Bodirsky, Martin, and Mottet in 2018. Following their approach, we give a self-contained proof of this classification, correcting several errors in the argument. We further show that, with the exception of cases arising from finite-domain CSPs, all tractable cases are solved by a well-known uniform algorithm, eliminating the need for the collection of ad-hoc algorithms used in the original paper. A central component of the proof allows the analysis to be restricted to first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$ that contain the successor relation. We substantially simplify this reduction and generalize the underlying construction. This generalization allows us to apply the same technique to first-order reducts of the triangular lattice graph and of infinite regular trees, yielding a complete complexity classification for these classes of structures, in particular a $\mathsf{P}$ versus $\mathsf{NP}$-complete dichotomy.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Pieper

item.title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.22002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.
item.dc:creator: Connor Watson

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.22205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paradigm of a simple unstable theory in the sense of Shelah is the theory of the random graph, the Fra\"iss\'e limit of the finite graphs. Quantum error correction has a paradigm of its own, and we show that it is the counterpart of the random graph: the Pauli group on countably many qubits, taken modulo phases and with commutation as its relation, is the Fra\"iss\'e limit of the finite alternating spaces over the two-element field, and its form computes the syndromes of stabilizer codes. Seen through this correspondence, simplicity theory turns out to be a theory of error correction. Clifford encoding circuits implement the homogeneity of the Pauli group, forking recognizes the logical errors, and the independence theorem of Kim and Pillay is the gluing of syndromes. The two paradigms look alike as first-order structures, and they part company only when observables enter. Each defines a bipartite observable, and we prove that, once preparations are mixed, both acquire the tree property of the second kind in real-valued logic. They reach it by different roads, however, and we show that the probes decide which. The probes of the Pauli observable are the Pauli channels; for them the indicator of each syndrome sector is the difference of the responses of two uniform mixtures, and actual mixtures already witness the tree. The probes of the Rado observable see only marginals; conditions given by actual mixtures remain compatible on disjoint blocks, and the tree must be sought among idealized preparations.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~{n}ez, Jos\'{e} Iovino

item.title: Differential equations as difference-differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the behavior of systems of algebraic differential equations when considered as systems of difference-differential equations, with special emphasis on systems which define minimal sets relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCF}$ of differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ distinguished commuting derivations. We show that if $p$ is a minimal type relative to $\operatorname{DCF}$ defined by a system of algebraic partial differential equations and inequations and the forking geometry on $p$ is trivial (also called ``disintegrated''), then $p$ remains minimal when regarded as a partial type relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCFA}$ of difference-differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ commuting derivations in the sense that every completion has $\operatorname{SU}$-rank one. We illustrate this theorem by describing in detail the possible difference-differential equations consistent with differential equations of the form $y' = y^3 + a_2 y^2 + a_1 y + a_0$ where $a_0$, $a_1$, and $a_2$ are differential constants.
item.dc:creator: Wei Li, Thomas Scanlon

item.title: The rank problem for metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a complete, second countable metric space with uncountable Scott rank. This answers a well-known question posed by Fokina, Friedman, K{\"o}rwien and Nies, and shows that the known upper bound $\omega_1$ on the rank, proved by Doucha, is sharp. Further, a Baire category based variant of the rank of metric spaces is developed, and this is used to give new proofs of the known rank bounds based only on standard methods of descriptive set theory.
item.dc:creator: Asger Tornquist

item.title: 86 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
item.description: arXiv:2610.20691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $f(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $f(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{86}\in\mathbb Q$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Normalization by Evaluation with Substitutions as Operations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In previous works on normalization by evaluation (NbE) with an untyped domain model, explicit substitutions are a major decision choice, which, in retrospect, is taken to simplify subsequent semantic proofs. This choice hence is taken for a purely technical reason. In addition, there is no obvious lemma to test the completeness of the definition or the laws for explicit substitutions. In this technical report, we investigate NbE in a typical setting, i.e. defining substitutions as operations. We show that this setting brings simplifications in proving syntactic properties and soundness of NbE, though complications are introduced in the completeness proof of NbE.
item.dc:creator: Jason Z. S. Hu

item.title: B\'ezout bounds and rational points on quasianalytic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For functions $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $\mathcal C_M$, we establish explicit bounds for the number of intersection points of the graph $\Gamma(f)$ with algebraic curves of degree at most $d$. The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $\Gamma(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $\Gamma(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.
item.dc:creator: Armin Rainer

item.title: An undecidable problem in dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a variety $X$ with a self-map $\phi$ and subvarieties $Y$ and $Z$ of $X$, we consider the set of $n$ for which $\phi^n(Y)$ intersects $Z$ nontrivially. Extending a beautiful construction of Lee and Nam, we show this gives rise to an undecidable problem for a fixed ambient variety $X$ and morphism $\phi$. We further use this construction to give a counterexample to a conjecture of the author, Satriano, and Sierra.
item.dc:creator: Jason Bell

item.title: Extended Frege proofs, circuits and rewriting
item.description: arXiv:2606.13367v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inspired by a statement about Extended Frege proof systems by Jain and Jin (FOCS 2022) we prove that: - there is a p-time binary relation $\approx$ between circuits that implies their logical equivalence, - if the equivalence $C \equiv D$ has an Extended Frege or a Circuit Frege proof with $k$ steps then there is a chain of circuits $E_i$ $$ C = E_0 \approx \dots \approx E_t = D $$ with $t \le O(k \log k)$, and the total size of the chain is bounded above by $(k+|C|+|D|)^{O(1)}$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Krajicek

item.title: Canonical expansions of $\mathbb R_{\mathcal Q}$-germs
item.description: arXiv:2609.13189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ be the field of unary germs at $0^+$ definable in the quasianalytic o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ of Kaiser-Rolin-Speissegger. We construct a canonical ordered differential-field embedding of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ into the field of natural-support generalized Laurent series. Every unary germ has a unique such asymptotic expansion, and bounded germs have expansions with only nonnegative exponents. A germ admits a convergent generalized Laurent-series representation exactly when its canonical expansion converges; in that case, every convergent representation with well-ordered support is canonical. We also prove that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ is branching in the sense of Dembner [1]. A nonresonant hyperbolic saddle with divergent Dulac series yields a bounded positive real-analytic $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-definable germ whose canonical generalized power series diverges. This gives a negative answer to a question of Dembner asking whether every unary germ definable in a branching structure admits a convergent generalized power-series representation. Nevertheless, every bounded unary $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-germ has a canonical formal generalized power-series expansion. Consequently, the convergent germs form a proper ordered differential subfield of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: Stoic Logic and Natural Term Logic
item.description: arXiv:2609.20665v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we propose a reconstruction of the theory of multiple generality in Stoic Logic using the Natural Term Logic (NTL) developped by the author in \cite{ntl}. Contrary to a frequent misconception, it can be shown conclusively, based on the available evidence, that Stoic logic was far more than a mere propositional logic (we further argue that even identifying the Stoic conditional with any type of propositional connective is misleading). Its more general and complex logical theory - and notable the treatment of multiple generality - was rather patterned after the logico-syntactic mechanisms of natural language (subject to a regimentation which recalls Polish notation) rather than the variable-based quantifier logic of the modern Fregean tradition. NTL is likewise is a variable-free formal framework which captures the core syntactic and logic mechanisms of natural language (and notably a large array of features involving intensionality and anaphoric constructions). Bobzien and Shogry \cite{bobzienshogry} have presented abundant evidence and arguments for the case that quantified conditionals and multiple generality were treated by the Stoics through a disambiguifying regimentation of syntax using indefinite pronouns and anaphoric constructions involving such pronouns. There are however some patent difficulties involving how exactly the equivalent of universal quantification was treated. In this paper we explore some possible building blocks for a formal reconstruction of the Stoic logic of multiple generality based on a variant of NTL. We focus on formalizing the more general form of Stoic modus ponens involving quantified conditions which was clearly attested by ancient authors. We also sketch, as a preliminary study for formalizing the grammatical theory deployed in Stoic logic, how NTL can be used to formalize adjectival and adverbial constructions.
item.dc:creator: Clarence Lewis Protin

item.title: The unbalanced graph of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations
item.description: arXiv:2510.04989v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the isomorphism of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the relation induced by the conjugacy action of the full group of an ergodic measure-preserving transformation on itself. This answers a question of Le Ma\^{i}tre in the negative and gives a positive indication towards a conjecture of Sabok. On the other hand, we prove that the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not unbalanced, which answers another question of Le Ma\^{i}tre in the negative. On the positive side, we prove that every two ergodic measure-preserving transformations are connected by a path of length two in the unbalanced graph on the set of ergodic measure-preserving transformations.
item.dc:creator: Bo Peng

item.title: Proofs Without Nominals: G\"odel's Ontological Argument, its Shallow Embedding, and the Open Questions of the Monatshefte Notes
item.description: arXiv:2609.36279v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzm\"uller and Scott's Notes on G\"odel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument, reaches beyond the modal object language: its quantifiers range over domains containing the nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic. A proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding, not necessarily of the modal logic. Whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled by replaying it in an explicit calculus, or, more cheaply and for all results at once, by analysing what the embedding's proofs substitute. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof in the embedding substituting nothing outside the object language, 294 of them explicit. The Notes' own proofs substitute none either; what it flags are terms a prover introduced. A soundness theorem over general models closed under the object language, and a sentence of that language the embedding proves but which fails in one of them, fix what the certificate says. The Notes' three open questions are settled too, without nominals, but by the empty instance of the conjunction axiom, too cheaply to convince. Generalised to G\"odel's "any number of summands", the axiom covers the empty conjunction and the singleton. This article restricts it to at least two different conjuncts, a non-degenerate reading of G\"odel's footnote, and settles them again without nominals. In effect only the empty conjunction is excluded; the singleton comes back with the other axioms. In one variant the restriction refutes the possible existence of a God-like being; the answers return, with no side condition, once the Notes' non-emptiness clause is confined to G\"odel's essence. Every theorem here is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4, the separating model in its propositional part; the countermodels are Nitpick's, checked by the build.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Benzm\"uller
